issues.description:
[bug-hunt] OS push-notification taps are DEAD (no deep-link) and foreground push toasts never fire, because the FE push handler reads the wrong FCM data-payload key. This is a DIFFERENT surface from i-20260719-7f3a (which fixed only the in-app /notifications list). 7f3a was filed on the FALSE premise that "the push-tap path DOES route every type" — it does not.

ROOT CAUSE (cross-repo key mismatch):
- Backend builds the FCM data payload with ONLY two keys: data_payload['notification_type'] and data_payload['notification_id'] (nyu_backend/backend.py:1304-1308 — the ONLY messaging.Message() in the whole backend, sent via create_notification -> send_push_notification). It never sends 'type', 'link', or 'message_id'.
- FE reads the WRONG keys: src/capacitor/push.ts pushNotificationActionPerformed line 233 does  notificationType = data.type || ''  , line 234  link = data.link  , line 235  messageId = data.message_id  . Backend sends key "notification_type", so data.type is ALWAYS undefined.

CONSEQUENCE:
1) Tap from OS tray: notificationType='' -> not weekly_review, not coach/admin, staticNotificationRoute('')=null, link='' -> NO branch matches -> requestNav() is never called -> the app opens but does NOT deep-link. EVERY push tap is a dead tap (workout/meal/water reminders, coach/admin/support messages, weekly_review, streak_risk, friend_request, health-score reminders, kudos, etc.).
2) Foreground receive: pushNotificationReceived (push.ts:178) also reads notification.data?.type -> the weekly_review / streak_risk / meal_reminder / workout_reminder in-app TOASTS never fire either.

So the shared route map introduced by 7f3a is INERT on the real OS push surface — the type never arrives under the key push.ts reads.

EXPECTED: tapping a push notification deep-links to the same screen the in-app list opens (e.g. weight_reminder -> /log-weight, meal_reminder -> /nutrition, coach_message -> /coach-chat).
ACTUAL: the tap opens the app on the default route only; no deep-link. Foreground reminder toasts are also absent.

REPRO: send any push (or inspect the FCM payload) -> data = {notification_type, notification_id}; in push.ts data.type is undefined -> handler falls through with no navigation. Verifiable from code in BOTH repos without a device.

FIX (minimal, FE): read the backend key -> notificationType = data.type || data.notification_type || ''  (at both push.ts:178 and :233). That restores all static-route + coach/admin(bare) + weekly_review deep-links immediately. FULL parity also needs the backend to forward link/message_id/date into data_payload (from the notification's meta_data) so message_id/link deep-links resolve too; e.g. add data_payload['type']=notification_type and copy meta_data link/message_id/date. Add a test asserting push.ts consumes the SAME key the backend emits so this can't drift again.

fix.description: Root cause: push notifications carried the type under the key 'notification_type', but the app read a different key ('type'), so the type was always empty -- every OS push tap opened the app with no deep-link and foreground reminder toasts never fired. Fix: the app now reads the correct key at both push handlers, and the backend also forwards routing hints (link/message_id/review_id), so tapping a push opens the SAME screen the in-app list does (meal reminder -> Nutrition, weight reminder -> Log Weight, coach message -> Coach Chat). Guarded by a new drift test so the key can't silently diverge again. Backend is live on production; the app-side fix ships in the next build.

issues.description:
[bug-hunt] Plate Calculator gives a WRONG breakdown + a false "not loadable" warning when the user configures a non-canonical set of available plates (via the plate editor / custom plates). Root cause: calcPlates() (src/components/PlateCalculatorSheet.tsx:67-100) loads the bar with a pure GREEDY largest-first algorithm, which is only optimal for the canonical default set [25,20,15,10,5,2.5,1.25]. On any set where greedy can get stuck, it (a) fails to find an EXACT solution that exists and (b) emits a plate list whose real sum contradicts the weight shown in the header/diagram.

EXPECTED: for target 80kg on a 20kg bar with available plates {20,15}, per side = 30kg = 15+15, so 80kg IS exactly loadable and the diagram should show two 15kg plates per side.
ACTUAL (code-proven via node, replicating calcPlates): calcPlates(80,20,[20,15]) => {plates:[20], isExact:false, nearestBelow:80, nearestAbove:110}. Greedy takes one 20 (largest), leaves 10 which nothing fills, and never backtracks to 15+15. So: (1) the amber "80 kg isn't exactly loadable" warning fires even though it IS loadable; (2) nearestBelow is reported as 80 while the breakdown it returns is a single 20kg plate/side = only 60kg total — the bar diagram + "= bar 20kg + per side" formula render ONE 20kg plate per side under an "80 kg" header (plates shown load 60, header says 80). The per-side footer shows 20.00 kg while nearestBelow implies 30/side.

REPRO: live workout -> open a set editor -> tap the Plate Calculator -> Settings2 (configure available plates) -> deselect everything except 20 and 15 (or add a custom plate that makes the set non-canonical) -> target 80kg. Shows false "not loadable" + a 20kg-only breakdown that does not match 80kg. (Default plate set is greedy-safe, so this only bites edited/custom configs — the plate editor explicitly supports both, i-20260702-plc8.)

FIX: replace greedy with an exhaustive/DP fill over the available plate multiset (or verify greedy reached perSide and fall back to a search when it did not), so the exact solution is found and nearestBelow/nearestAbove + the rendered plates always agree with the displayed weight.

It now finds the real solution, so 80kg correctly shows two 15kg plates per side and every number agrees. Proven by re-rendering the calculator with the exact repro config.

[bug-hunt] Add Food modal (CustomMealModal, Quick Log tab): tapping a "Recent" meal chip that has calories mislabels the re-logged meal as "AI estimated".

ROOT CAUSE (src/components/nutrition/CustomMealModal.tsx): fillFromRecent() (line ~266) writes the recent meal into photoMacros ({description: meal.meal_name, total_calories, ...}) — the SAME state slot the AI photo/text-estimate paths use. The result card at line ~678 renders whenever [ photoMacros && photoMacros.description === customMealText.trim() && photoMacros.total_calories > 0 ], and its label is hard-coded "AI estimated" (with estimateConfidence null it shows just "AI estimated", no confidence suffix). Nothing distinguishes a user-history recent meal from an actual AI estimate, so a re-logged recent meal is presented as an AI guess.

EXPECTED: re-logging a recent meal shows its exact historical macros with no "AI estimated" badge (those numbers are the user's own logged values, not an AI estimate).
ACTUAL: the purple "AI estimated" card appears over a recent meal's real macros, implying the numbers are an AI guess.

REPRO: 1) /nutrition -> tap "Log Meal"/"Add Food" (open CustomMealModal). 2) In the Quick Log tab, tap a chip under "Recent" that shows a kcal value. 3) The description fills and a purple "AI estimated" card renders below the Estimate-with-AI button — even though the meal came from history, not AI.

FIX: track the macro source (e.g. a separate estimateSource: "ai" | "recent" | null, or a boolean set only by the AI paths) and gate the "AI estimated" badge on the AI source; recent-meal prefill should show a neutral/no badge. NOTE: data is fine (re-logging the historical macros is correct) — this is a label-only mislabel.

issues.description:
[bug-hunt] "Your Week's Plan" (DietPlanWeek) lets you mark a FUTURE day's meal as eaten, inflating weekly progress/streak with food not yet eaten. 

ROOT CAUSE (src/pages/DietPlanWeek.tsx): the per-meal eaten toggle (DayCard onToggleMeal -> toggleMeal.mutate -> nutritionService.logMeal) has NO date guard — it fires for any day whose card shows meals, regardless of isPast/isToday. The feature's own comment (line ~57) scopes intent to "today OR a past day the user forgot to mark", but the code never enforces it. The backend materializes the WHOLE current week up front (plan_generator materialize loop: mat_start = this week's Monday, mat_days up to 7), so on any weekday except Sunday the future days of the current week already have real AssignedMeal rows with valid assigned_meal_id. Expanding a future day and tapping a meal toggles is_eaten server-side for a date that hasn't happened. weekly.mealsEaten and weekly.daysComplete (the "Streak / full days" stat) then count those future meals.

EXPECTED: only today's and past days' meals are markable as eaten; future-day meal rows are non-interactive (disabled toggle / read-only).
ACTUAL: future-day meal toggles are active; tapping marks a not-yet-eaten future meal as eaten and inflates the week's progress + full-days count.

REPRO: 1) On any weekday other than Sunday, open /diet-plan-week (Profile -> progress, or Plan Timeline -> "Diet Plan"). 2) Expand a day LATER in the week that shows meals. 3) Tap a meal's target/circle button -> it flips to a green "eaten" check with no restriction. 4) "This Week's Progress" Meals + Streak stats increase for a day that hasn't occurred.

FIX: in DayCard, disable the eaten toggle (and drop the "tap a meal" hint) when the bucket is in the future (bucket dt > today); only allow toggling for isToday || isPast.

fix.description: Root cause: 'Your Week's Plan' let you tap a FUTURE day's meal as eaten. Because the backend fills in the whole current week ahead of time, those future meals were real and tappable, so marking one wrongly counted toward your weekly meals + full-days streak. Fix: future-day meals are now shown but not tappable, with an 'Upcoming — you can mark these off once the day arrives' note; only today's and past days' meals can be marked eaten (past-day backfill still works).

issues.description:
[bug-hunt] Live workout player: after tapping "Continue" on the auto-advance banner (or when the final set POST resolves), the NEXT exercise's set editor opens with a rest timer already counting down — carried over from the PREVIOUS exercise — and when it elapses it logs a rest duration against the WRONG (previous) exercise.

ROOT CAUSE (src/pages/Activity.tsx): handleContinueToNext() (the "Continue -> next exercise" banner tap) closes the current ExerciseWheelPicker and reopens it for the next exercise, but never resets showRestTimer. logSetMutation.onSuccess arms the rest timer (setShowRestTimer(true)) whenever isModalOpen.current is true; the picker's own onClose resets it (setShowRestTimer(false)) but handleContinueToNext bypasses onClose and directly flips showWheelPicker. So showRestTimer stays true across the exercise switch. The next picker (key=new exercise_id) remounts and renders restTimerElement (gated only on showRestTimer), starting a fresh 90s countdown before any set is logged for the new exercise. Because lastLoggedSetRef.current still points at the PREVIOUS exercise's final set, the timer's onComplete/onSkip fires activityService.logSet({exercise_id: last.exercise_id=PREVIOUS, ...rest_seconds}) — writing rest_seconds to the wrong exercise while the user is on the new one, and speakRestCue announces the wrong set. (Same outcome if the final-set POST resolves after the picker has already advanced: onSuccess sees isModalOpen.current true and arms the timer in the new exercise's picker.)

EXPECTED: advancing to the next exercise starts it with NO active rest timer; the rest timer arms only after a set is logged for the exercise currently open, and any rest_seconds is attributed to that exercise.
ACTUAL: next exercise opens with a leftover running rest timer; on elapse it logs rest_seconds against the previous exercise and speaks a cue for the previous set.

REPRO: 1) Open Activity with a workout plan that has >=2 exercises. 2) Tap an exercise, log all its target sets via the wheel picker (rest timer arms after each set). 3) On the final set the "Set complete - next exercise" banner appears; tap Continue. 4) The next exercise's editor opens with a rest countdown already running (before logging anything). 5) Leave it ~90s: a background log-set POST fires for the PREVIOUS exercise (visible in network).

FIX: in handleContinueToNext (and ideally when adopting the next session in onSessionStarted), setShowRestTimer(false) + bump restTimerKey so the leftover timer is torn down; only re-arm on a set log for the newly-open exercise.

issues.description: [bug-hunt] Un-skipping a meal that was skipped in a PRIOR session gives no immediate visual feedback — the card stays struck-through/grayscale with the SKIPPED badge until a network refetch returns, even though a "Meal unskipped" toast fires instantly. Root cause: NutritionMealList.tsx:41 computes isSkipped = skippedMealIds.has(meal.assigned_meal_id) || !!meal.is_skipped. handleUnskipMeal (useNutritionData.tsx:376-382) only removes the id from the local skippedMealIds Set; it does NOT optimistically clear the cached is_skipped. skipMealMutation.onSuccess (line 323-326) merely invalidates [diet-plan]/[dashboard-overview] — no optimistic setQueryData flip. So when a meal was skipped in an earlier session, skippedMealIds is empty on load but the server payload sets meal.is_skipped=true (backend.py:7190/9551 from AssignedMeal.skipped_at); the local removal is overridden by the still-true cached is_skipped, so the OR keeps the card skipped for the whole round-trip. The SKIP direction works (adds to Set -> OR short-circuits true instantly); only UNSKIP is broken. Expected: card visually un-skips on tap (like skip does). Actual: card stays skipped until refetch; toast contradicts card state; reads as a dead tap on slow connections. Repro: (1) open /nutrition with an active diet plan, (2) skip a meal, (3) cold-reload the app so is_skipped comes from the server and skippedMealIds is empty, (4) tap Unskip on that meal -> no immediate change, toast says unskipped, card flips only after the diet-plan refetch. Fix: mirror logMealMutation.onMutate — optimistically setQueryData([diet-plan, today]) to flip the target meal is_skipped=false (with snapshot rollback in onError), OR seed skippedMealIds from server is_skipped so the Set is the single source of truth.

fix.description: Root cause: un-skipping a meal that was skipped in an EARLIER session only cleared a local flag, but the card's skipped look also came from the server copy of the plan — so it stayed struck-through with the SKIPPED badge until a background refresh landed, even though the 'Meal unskipped' toast fired instantly. Fix: the meal now un-skips (and skips) instantly on tap by updating the cached plan directly, with automatic rollback if the save fails. [bug-hunt] Nutrition intermittent-fasting banner: on a backend-flagged "intermittent" fasting day, tapping "End fast" does NOT stick on the first tap — the shared fast restarts itself within ~1s so the ring/timer reappears and the button feels dead. A second tap is needed.

ROUTE: /nutrition (FastingBanner)

ROOT CAUSE: src/pages/Nutrition.tsx:101-114 — the reconcile useEffect re-creates the shared stopwatch whenever there is NO active fast on a backend intermittent fasting day:
  if (!fastingDay || fastingType !== 'intermittent' || active) return;
  ... startFast('16:8', 16, start);
Its deps are [fastingDay, fastingType, active, startFast].
handleEndFast (Nutrition.tsx:127-131) does: endFast() (clears the shared active -> active=null) then onSetFasting(false,null).
But onSetFasting is NOT optimistic: useNutritionData.tsx:392-405 fires setFastingMutation and only flips fastingDay/fastingType via refetchFasting() in onSuccess (fastingDay derives from the server query cache, useNutritionData.tsx:512-513). So immediately after End: active=null but fastingDay is STILL true and fastingType STILL 'intermittent'.
React re-renders on active->null, the effect re-runs, the guard is false (fastingDay true, type intermittent, active null), computeBackdatedStart() resolves, loadActive() is null, and startFast() re-arms the fast the user just ended.

WHY THE RACE RELIABLY LOSES: the resurrect path needs ONE round-trip (2 parallel getDailyLogs in computeBackdatedStart). The cancel path needs TWO sequential round-trips (POST setFastingStatus -> then GET getFastingStatus refetch) before fastingDay flips to false and the effect cleanup sets cancelled=true. One trip beats two, so the restart wins at normal latency.

REPRO:
1. On /nutrition tap the 'Intermittent' fasting-day chip (sets backend fasting_day=true, type=intermittent -> shared 16:8 stopwatch auto-starts, ring shows).
2. Tap 'End fast'.
3. EXPECTED: the fasting strip/ring disappears and stays gone.
4. ACTUAL: the ring vanishes then re-appears within ~1s (fast restarted). Only a SECOND 'End fast' tap (after the backend flag has flipped) actually ends it.

FIX: the reconcile effect must not resurrect a fast the user just ended. Options: (a) set a local 'endedToday' ref in handleEndFast and short-circuit the reconcile effect while set for today; (b) make onSetFasting optimistic (setQueryData ['fasting-status', today] to fasting_day:false immediately so fastingDay flips synchronously); (c) only auto-start in the reconcile effect on mount, not on every active-goes-null transition.

Now ending a fast marks it ended for the day so it will not auto-restart, and the first tap sticks. Added a regression test.

issues.description:
[bug-hunt] Badge-unlock toast dedup is keyed on the badge's display NAME, not its id/key — a real second unlock in the same check can be silently swallowed (no toast, no error).

WHERE: src/components/achievement-context.tsx:211-218 —
```js
const shownBadgesRef = useRef<Set<string>>(new Set());
const showAchievement = useCallback((payload) => {
  if (shownBadgesRef.current.has(payload.badgeName)) return;
  shownBadgesRef.current.add(payload.badgeName);
  ...
```
Dedup uses `payload.badgeName` (display text). The caller (src/hooks/useGamification.ts:62-64) builds the payload from checkBadges() results using only `name`, `tier`, `xp`, `icon_url` — it never threads through a stable `badge_key`/id.

This is the same class of bug LevelCard.tsx already had and was fixed for (badgeCount now dedupes by badge_key to match the Achievements gallery's earnedByKey — commit 0ff6345a, 2026-07-15) but this second site was missed. If checkBadges() ever returns two distinct badges in one call whose display names collide (e.g. two tiers of the same badge family sharing a base name, or any backend name-string collision), the second real unlock never shows a toast — it's marked 'shown' the instant the first one's name is added to the Set, even though it's a different badge.

EXPECTED: every distinct badge unlock (by id/key) gets its own toast, exactly once.
ACTUAL: unlocks colliding on display name after the first are dropped silently.

FIX: thread badge_key (or badge id) through AchievementPayload from useGamification.ts's checkBadges() call, and key shownBadgesRef on that instead of badgeName.
issues.author: shakeebshaan

fix.description: Root cause: badge-unlock toasts were de-duplicated by the badge's display NAME, so if two different badges shared a display name in the same unlock check, the second real unlock was silently swallowed (no toast). Fix: de-dup now keys on each badge's stable key (falling back to the name for keyless callers), so every distinct badge unlock shows its own toast exactly once. This is a logic fix with no visible screen change, so the attached proof is a summary card (root cause + fix + regression test).

When meta_data.link is absent it falls to a switch on notification.type; there is NO case for these persisted types, so they hit `default: break` and never navigate. getIconForType/getColorForType also lack them, so the rows render a generic gray Bell icon.

issues.description:
[bug-hunt] Weekly-review runs TWO decision-tree engines back-to-back and MERGES their proposed changes, but they use DIFFERENT field-name vocabularies, so the dedup misses collisions -> duplicate/contradictory calorie cards (both applied, last-wins) + a steps card that never applies.

WHERE: app/services/weekly_review.py:440-490 runs weekly_review_engine.analyze_week() (main) then adjustment_engine.generate_weekly_adjustment() (adjustment) each nightly review + on /reviews routes (routes/reviews.py:116,225). The merge de-dups adjustment changes against the main set by the `field` key:
    existing_fields = {c.get("field") for c in engine_changes}
    for ac in adj_changes: if ac.get("field") not in existing_fields: engine_changes.append(ac)   (weekly_review.py:487-490)
But the two engines name the SAME concept differently:
  * Calories: main field="target_calories" (weekly_review_engine.py:775) vs adjustment field="calories" (adjustment_engine.py:186/306/388/447). BOTH carry category="calories".
  * Steps: main field="daily_steps_goal" (weekly_review_engine.py:749) vs adjustment field="steps_goal" (adjustment_engine.py:272). BOTH carry category="activity".

EXPECTED: one shared field vocabulary (or dedup by category/concept) so a single calorie/step change is proposed and applied.
ACTUAL:
(1) DUPLICATE CALORIE CARDS, BOTH APPLIED: for a stalled fat-loss user w/ good adherence both engines fire (main decision_path=plateau_step1/2, adjustment change_type=stall_intervention). decision_path != on_track so the merge takes the `elif adj_changes` branch; adjustment field "calories" is NOT in {target_calories,carbs_g,fat_g} -> appended. proposed_changes now has TWO category=calories cards w/ different targets (e.g. 2000->1900 from main AND 2000->1850 from adjustment). The Monday applier _apply_macro_change (weekly_review.py:1169) dispatches on category=="calories" -> macros.calories_kcal=int(value), so BOTH apply and the LAST (adjustment, appended last) silently overrides. User sees two conflicting Calories X->Y cards; the "N of M changes will take effect" toast overcounts.
(2) DEAD STEPS CARD: _apply_activity_changes (weekly_review.py:1091-1110) only handles field=="daily_steps_goal"; the adjustment engine's field=="steps_goal" hits the else -> logger.warning("Unknown activity field: steps_goal") and is NEVER applied. So an adjustment step-goal proposal is shown to the user but silently discarded on apply.

REPRO (code trace): fat_loss plan, 2+ weekly reviews with weight within noise, adherence>=80%, review.avg_daily_steps populated -> both engines emit calorie/step changes -> weekly_review.py:487 appends adjustment's "calories"+"steps_goal" alongside main's "target_calories"+"daily_steps_goal" -> apply doubles the calorie change (last wins) and drops the steps one.

FIX: unify the field names across the two engines (adjustment -> target_calories / daily_steps_goal), OR dedup by category instead of field. NOT a dup of w7q3 (that was the applier ignoring per-change deselection); this is the engine-merge producing duplicate/dead changes upstream.

fix.description: Root cause: the adjustment engine named calorie/step changes with a different field vocabulary (field 'calories'/'steps_goal') than the main engine ('target_calories'/'daily_steps_goal'), so weekly_review.py's field-based merge dedup missed the collision — two contradictory calorie cards both applied (last-wins) and the steps card hit 'Unknown activity field' and never applied. Fix: extracted RULE 3 into _stall_intervention() and renamed every calorie/step field to the main engine's vocabulary so the merge collapses to a single calorie/step change and the steps card is applied. Verified: TestStallVocabulary 5/5 green; 221 related weekly-review tests green; deployed to prod (834cd7f), health OK.

issues.description:
[bug-hunt] Weekly adjustment engine's stall protocol jumps straight to a CALORIE CUT (with a false "steps not tracked" message) for fat-loss users who ARE tracking steps at/above their goal but below the 12k ceiling.

WHERE: app/services/adjustment_engine.py RULE 3 stall-intervention branch (lines ~259-374). The NEAT-first tiering is:
    if avg_steps < current_steps_goal:            -> propose step increase (Step 1)   (:269)
    elif avg_steps >= STEP_TARGET_CEILING(12000): -> reduce calories (Step 2)          (:290)
    else:  # comment: "Steps data not available, go straight to calorie reduction"     (:349)
           -> 100 kcal cut + insight "Track step count so we can use NEAT increases in the future"

The `else` fires not only when steps are genuinely absent, but ALSO when avg_steps IS present and either (a) current_steps_goal is None (no ActivityTarget row), or (b) avg_steps >= goal but < 12000 (e.g. goal 8000, user averaging 9000).

EXPECTED: when steps are tracked and sit between the goal and the 12k ceiling, propose raising the step TARGET toward 12k first (the engine's own "increase NEAT before touching calories" tier), and never print "Steps data not available"/"Track step count" when review.avg_daily_steps exists.
ACTUAL: immediate calorie reduction + misleading "not tracked" copy, even though review.avg_daily_steps is populated (weekly_review.py:517). These feed real proposed_changes that auto-apply Monday.

REPRO (code trace): fat_loss stalled user, adherence>=80%, review.avg_daily_steps=9000, ActivityTarget.daily_steps_goal=8000 -> RULE 3: first if false (9000>=8000), elif false (9000<12000) -> else branch -> 100 kcal cut + "Track step count...". Code-proven; adjustment_engine is live via weekly_review.py:458 nightly generation + routes/reviews.py.

FIX: split the else into (i) genuinely-no-steps (avg_steps is None) -> keep current copy, and (ii) steps present but >= goal and < ceiling -> propose stepping the goal toward STEP_TARGET_CEILING before any calorie cut.
issues.author: shakeebshaan

fix.description: Root cause: the stall-protocol's final else cut ~100 kcal and printed 'Track step count / steps not tracked' whenever steps WERE present but sat between the daily goal and the 12k NEAT ceiling (e.g. goal 8000, averaging 9000), or when no ActivityTarget row existed — so a step-tracking fat-loss user got an immediate calorie cut with a false 'not tracked' message. Fix (adjustment_engine.py RULE 3): split the else — steps tracked & below ceiling now propose raising daily_steps_goal toward 12k (NEAT before calories) and never print the 'not tracked' copy; only avg_steps==None keeps the conservative calorie cut + track-steps prompt. Verified: TestStallNeatFirst fail-before (3 failed) / pass-after (4 passed); 221 related weekly-review tests green; deployed to prod (834cd7f), health OK.

issues.description:
[bug-hunt] Weekly Review "Approve N of M" (deselect changes) is silently ignored — the Monday auto-apply job applies ALL originally-proposed changes regardless of what the user kept.

Expected: deselecting a proposed change then tapping "Approve N of M" applies ONLY the kept changes to next week (the UI even promises "N of M changes will take effect Monday").
Actual: every AI-proposed change is applied to week N+1 anyway; the deselected ones take effect too.

Root cause (traced both repos):
- FE AcceptChangesFlow.tsx: each ProposedChange.id is the index into proposed_changes (backend reviews.py _normalize_proposed_changes sets id=str(i)). Deselecting + tapping the primary button fires handleSubmit("approve_selected") with approved_change_ids = Array.from(selectedIds) (the kept subset).
- review.service.ts:144 maps approve_selected -> POST /reviews/:id/modify { modified_changes: approved_change_ids }.
- Backend modify_review (app/routes/reviews.py:317) stores review.user_modified_changes = modified_changes and sets status="reviewed"; it does NOT prune review.proposed_changes.
- Monday job weekly_plan_apply (app/services/weekly_review.py:825) processes status in (reviewed, notified); it loads proposed = json.loads(review.proposed_changes) (the FULL original list, line 857) and applies EVERY item via _apply_macro_change / _apply_activity_changes (lines 895-908). It NEVER reads review.user_modified_changes.

So a user who explicitly rejects e.g. an aggressive calorie cut still gets it applied to next week WeeklyMacroTarget; the "N of M changes will take effect Monday" toast (AcceptChangesFlow.tsx:56) is false.

Repro: active plan with a generated weekly review having 2+ proposed changes -> open /weekly-review -> deselect one change -> tap "Approve N of M" -> Monday weekly_plan_apply applies all proposed changes to week N+1.

Fix: in weekly_plan_apply, when review.user_modified_changes is set (modify path), filter proposed to only the indices listed in user_modified_changes before applying (change ids are str(index) into proposed_changes). reject_all is already handled (status stays / no apply), but partial-select currently behaves identically to approve_all.
issues.author: shakeebshaan

fix.description: Root cause: the Monday auto-apply job applied every AI-proposed weekly-review change to next week no matter what you chose, so deselecting a change in Approve N of M (or rejecting the review outright) still applied it. Fix: the job now honors your choice: approve-selected applies only the changes you kept, a full reject applies nothing (next week stays a clean copy of this week), and approve-all still applies everything. Backend fix deployed to prod with regression tests.

issues.description:
[bug-hunt] AI "Customize Meal" leaves the user with an un-appliable meal preview (dead-end).

The ONLY Apply/Discard controls live in the floating "Macro change" bar, which is gated on a non-null macro delta: `{macroDelta && updatedMeal && (...)}` (AIMealCustomization.tsx:531). The preview card itself carries NO buttons (comment at :517-520: "Apply/Discard live ONLY in the floating macro-delta bar"), and the text input is hidden whenever a preview exists via `{!updatedMeal && (...)}` (:582).

`macroDelta` (useMemo :269-280) returns null in two reachable cases:
1. No original snapshot: `originalMeal` stays null when the backend start payload omits `meal` AND the first `updated_meal` omits `original` (both optional in the UpdatedMeal type, ai.service.ts:410-427; the code even guards `if (!originalMeal && result.updated_meal.original)` :209, and the start comment :146-148 says only "some sessions" include the seed meal). 2. Zero delta: an AI change that keeps macros identical (e.g. a like-for-like veg swap, or a rename/description-only edit) yields exact 0/0/0/0 deltas -> suppressed (:278).

Actual: preview with no actionable control -> stuck.

issues.description:
[bug-hunt] AI Overview (/ai/overview) — the Weight tile paints its weekly-change trend arrow with a LOSS-BIASED good/bad color that ignores the user’s goal direction, so for a muscle-gain / weight-gain goal it is semantically inverted.

Root cause: weightChangeIndicator() (src/pages/AIOverview.tsx:43-47) hardcodes, regardless of goal_type:
  change < -0.1  -> text-success (green), ArrowDown   (weight DOWN treated as good)
  change >  0.1  -> text-destructive (red), ArrowUp   (weight UP treated as bad)
The returned color is applied to the trend arrow icon at AIOverview.tsx:379 (<WInd className={... wInd.color} />).

Expected: for a user whose goal is to GAIN (goal_type muscle_gain, or goal_weight above current), gaining should read as ON-TRACK (green) and losing as OFF-TRACK. The primary Dashboard weight card is already goal-progress-framed (start->now->goal milestone track, QA i-20260617-86ba) and is NOT loss-biased; this tile diverges.

Actual: a weight-gain user who successfully gains sees a RED (destructive) up-arrow implying the gain is bad; if they lose weight they get a GREEN “good” down-arrow. Color is the good/bad state signal here and it is wrong-signed for the entire gaining segment.

Open /ai/overview -> the Weight tile’s trend arrow renders red/destructive even though the gain is the desired direction (and a loss would render green).

Fix: make weightChangeIndicator goal-aware — take the goal direction (from dashboard-overview / profile goal_type or goal vs current weight) and map toward-goal -> success, away-from-goal -> destructive, near-zero -> neutral. The text label (↑/↓ x kg this week) can stay; only the color semantics must follow the goal. Low severity: color-only, the number itself is correct; IST/loss-goal users unaffected.

issues.description:

Root cause: date labels are built with new Date("YYYY-MM-DD"), which parses a bare date string as UTC midnight; toLocaleDateString / the recency compare then shift it back a day in any timezone west of UTC.
- DashboardSleepCard.recencyLabel  (src/pages/_components/dashboard/DashboardSleepCard.tsx:26)  ->  new Date(latestDate).toLocaleDateString(...)
- SleepQualityChart.formatLabel    (src/components/charts/SleepQualityChart.tsx:32)             ->  new Date(dateStr).toLocaleDateString(...)  (every X-axis label)

Expected: a night logged/synced on Jul 16 shows "Jul 16".
Actual (e.g. America/Los_Angeles, UTC-7): shows "Jul 15"; the Today/Last-night recency check can also mis-classify near midnight.

The codebase already fixed this exact class elsewhere: DashboardFastingCard uses new Date(`${date}T00:00:00`) (local) and lib/cycle.ts uses Date.UTC on split parts. The newer sleep code (i-20260716-sl33) reintroduced the naive parse.

Same naive pattern (wrong WEEKDAY label) also in: src/components/charts/StepsActivityChart.tsx:26, MacroAdherenceChart.tsx:26, CalorieBalanceChart.tsx:26.

Fix: parse the YYYY-MM-DD as local before formatting (append T00:00:00, or split+Date.UTC then format) — ideally add a shared parseLocalDate() helper in src/lib/date.ts and use it in all label formatters. Correct for IST (UTC+5:30) today, so India users are unaffected; only surfaces west of UTC.

Repro: set browser/device TZ to America/Los_Angeles, log or Health-Connect-sync sleep for 2+ days, open /dashboard — the Sleep card’s most-recent date reads one day earlier than logged.

issues.description:
[bug-hunt] Body Measurements ignores an imperial user’s unit_preference when the profile cache is cold — the cm/inch default fix is incomplete.

What’s wrong: src/pages/Measurements.tsx seeds the unit toggle ONCE at mount by reading the React-Query cache for key [profile-basic-info] (L78-81): cached?.unit_preference === imperial ? inch : cm. But this component never FETCHES [profile-basic-info] — it queries [user-profile] (L95-99, profileService.getProfile) and [measurements-overview]. There is NO effect that re-derives `unit` once the profile resolves. So when the [profile-basic-info] cache is empty at mount, an imperial user is shown centimetres and stays on cm until they manually toggle.

Expected vs actual: An imperial (unit_preference=imperial) user opening Measurements should default to inch. Actual: defaults to cm whenever [profile-basic-info] wasn’t already cached by a prior screen.

The recent fix (commit 595b3015 “Measurements cm/inch default respects unit_preference”, +5/-1 lines) added only the cache read — it works when the cache is warm (e.g. after visiting Profile/LogWeight which DO fetch that key) but does nothing on a cold cache. The comment on L77 claims it ‘mirrors LogWeight.tsx’, but LogWeight actually (a) fetches [profile-basic-info] itself (LogWeight.tsx L158-162) AND (b) has a one-shot sync effect (L224-233, `unitInitDone` ref) that calls handleUnitChange(lb) once profileData loads imperial. Measurements copied the cache-init but not the fetch + sync, so it self-corrects only by luck of a warm cache.

Repro: cold app start (or hard refresh) navigating directly to /measurements as an imperial user, with no prior screen having loaded [profile-basic-info] → toggle shows cm. Note: saved values are always canonical cm so no data corruption; this is a display-default bug.

Fix: mirror LogWeight fully — read unit_preference from the [user-profile] query this component already runs (or fetch [profile-basic-info]) and set `unit` in a one-shot effect when the profile resolves, guarded so it never overrides a manual toggle.

fix.description: Root cause: ChoosePlan computed the weight delta as Math.max(0, current − goal), which clamps to 0 for a weight-GAIN goal — so the header read 'up to 0 kg' and the recommended-plan badge showed '0 kg'. Fix: use the absolute magnitude with direction-aware copy (a new 'to gain' header variant across en/hi/hinglish/xx-AE) and hide the framing when the delta rounds to 0. Verified live on /choose-plan with a 70→80 kg gain goal: the header now reads 'up to 10 kg to gain' and the badge '10 kg', with a rising projection.

issues.description:
[bug-hunt] Choose Plan shows “up to 0 kg” in the header and a “0 kg” badge for weight-GAIN / muscle-gain goals.

What’s wrong: src/pages/ChoosePlan.tsx L403 computes kgsToLose = hasWeightProjection ? Math.max(0, currentWeightKg - goalWeightKg) : 0. For a gain goal (goalWeightKg > currentWeightKg) that subtraction is negative and Math.max clamps it to 0. That 0 is then rendered in two user-visible places:
  • Header (L912-914): t(choose_plan.header.title_with_goal, { count: Math.round(kgsToLose) }) → en.json L1407 “Pick your plan · up to {{count}} kg” → “Pick your plan · up to 0 kg”.
  • Recommended-card badge (L1046): {Math.round(kgsToLose)} kg → “0 kg”.

Expected vs actual: A user whose goal is to gain (e.g. current 70 kg → goal 80 kg) should see their 10 kg journey (or neutral copy), not “up to 0 kg”. The projection chart just below is direction-correct (it plots current→goal as a rising curve and its aria uses a loss/change split, L1171), so the header contradicts the chart on the same screen.

Repro: onboard/set a weight-gain or muscle-gain goal with current < goal weight, reach /choose-plan (paywall) → header reads “Pick your plan · up to 0 kg” and the recommended card badge reads “0 kg”. Loss goals are unaffected (positive delta).

Root cause: kgsToLose is loss-biased. Fix: use Math.abs(currentWeightKg - goalWeightKg) for the magnitude and make the header/badge copy direction-aware (lose vs gain), or hide the “up to X kg” framing for gain/maintain goals.

[suggestion] Add a per-day "Fasting/Vrat day" toggle on the Nutrition page that switches meal suggestions to religious-fast-appropriate dishes. Problem: a huge share of Indian users observe recurring food-restriction fasting days (Navratri, Ekadashi, Karva Chauth, Mondays for some) where grains/onion/garlic/certain veg are off-limits, but NYUS meal suggestions/swap picker have no concept of this and keep recommending regular roti/rice/dal meals on those days, breaking the precision-tool trust for a recurring, predictable use case. Evidence: src/data/meal-catalog.json already has 45+ vrat-named dishes (Sabudana Khichdi, Kuttu Atta items, Navratan preparations, singhara-based dishes) sitting dormant as plain catalog entries with zero dietary-restriction tag or filter hook - the data exists, the filtering doesn't. Existing fasting UI (FastingTrendChart) is unrelated (16:8 time-restricted eating, not food-type fasting). v1 scope: single day-scoped toggle chip near the Nutrition date header ("Fasting today") that (a) filters the meal-suggestion/swap picker lists to catalog items already identifiable as vrat-appropriate by name/ingredient keyword match, (b) suppresses grain-heavy default suggestions for that day only, (c) persists as a simple per-date client flag - no calendar/recurrence settings, no plan regeneration, no backend schema change. Effort: small-medium, ~2-3 days (keyword-tag pass over catalog + filter logic in the meal suggestion component + one persisted per-day preference + i18n strings across en/hi/hinglish).

issues.description:
[bug-hunt] Body Measurements save-failure handler calls an undefined function -> ReferenceError instead of the intended error toast.

What's wrong: src/pages/Measurements.tsx line 244 (logMeasurementMutation.onError) does  description: apiErrorMessage(error) ?? "Please try again." , but apiErrorMessage is NOT imported in this file - line 8 imports only { apiErrorRaw } from '@/lib/api-error'. apiErrorMessage is a real export of that module (api-error.ts:38) but is never imported here and not defined locally.

Proof: npx tsc -b reports  src/pages/Measurements.tsx(244,22): error TS2304: Cannot find name 'apiErrorMessage'.  It still ships because npm run build is a vite/esbuild build with no typecheck (same class + gotcha as i-20260716-1d76 / i-20260621-8625).

Expected vs actual: on a failed measurement save (network error / 5xx / offline / validation) the user should get the destructive toast 'Couldn't save measurement'. Instead, evaluating the toast() argument throws ReferenceError: apiErrorMessage is not defined before toast() is invoked, so NO error toast renders and the failure surfaces only as an uncaught console error. captureException (line 240, which uses the imported apiErrorRaw) still runs, so the crash is silent to the user.

Repro: open /measurements, pick a body part, enter a value, force the POST /measurements to fail (offline or 500), tap 'Save measurement'. Console shows ReferenceError; no toast appears.

Fix: add apiErrorMessage to the line-8 import: import { apiErrorMessage, apiErrorRaw } from '@/lib/api-error';

fix.description: Root cause: Measurements.tsx's save-failure handler called apiErrorMessage(error) for the toast description, but only apiErrorRaw was imported from @/lib/api-error — so a failed save threw ReferenceError before toast() ran and the user got NO error, only a silent console error. Fix: import apiErrorMessage (a real export of that module) alongside apiErrorRaw. Proof: forcing POST /measurements/log to 500 now renders the destructive 'Couldn't save measurement' toast with the server's message.

judge.note: Behavioral proof: the previously-silent save failure now surfaces the intended destructive toast (would have thrown ReferenceError before the import); full-screen authenticated /measurements capture, test gate green.

issues.description:
[bug-hunt] Weekly Progress 'TRENDS' chart - the Weight row of the multi-metric bar chart renders near-identical full-height bars that convey no trend, because weight is normalized against a zero baseline.

What's wrong: src/components/progress/MultiMetricBarChart.tsx BarRow (L88-95) sets maxValue = max value across the week, then each bar height = value / maxValue (L126-130). That zero-baseline normalization is right for count-like metrics (calories 0-2500, workouts 0/1) but wrong for weight, whose day-to-day variation is a tiny fraction of its absolute value. For a realistic week of e.g. 80.9-82.0 kg, bar heights come out 98.7%-100% - differences under 1px on the 48px-tall bar area, so every weight bar looks identical and the row shows no day-to-day movement.

Context: MultiMetricBarChart is the only bar chart actually rendered (WeeklyProgress.tsx:820, 'Daily breakdown' / 'TRENDS' section; the standalone WeightTrendChart/CalorieBalanceChart/StepsActivityChart/MacroAdherenceChart are barrel-exported but not mounted anywhere). The repo already has the correct pattern for weight: WeightTrendChart.tsx uses a windowed YAxis domain [floor(min-padding), ceil(max+padding)] (L108) so small weight deltas stay visible; the multi-metric weight row does not.

Expected vs actual: the Weight row should visibly reflect the week's ups/downs; actually it is a flat wall of ~full bars. (The per-day drilldown drawer shows the correct numeric value, so no data is lost - only the at-a-glance chart is uninformative.)

Fix: normalize the weight row against a windowed min-max domain (min-padding .. max+padding) like WeightTrendChart, instead of value/maxValue; or render weight as a line/sparkline rather than a zero-baseline bar.

fix.description: Root cause: the Weekly Progress TRENDS 'Daily breakdown' chart normalized every metric row against a zero baseline (height = value / weekMax). That's right for count-like metrics (calories, workouts) but wrong for weight, whose daily change is a tiny fraction of its absolute value — a realistic 80.9-82.0 kg week rendered near-identical ~98.7%-100% full-height bars, so the Weight row showed no trend. Fix: added a per-metric 'windowed' flag (weight only) that normalizes against a [min-pad, max+pad] domain like WeightTrendChart, so small weight deltas spread visibly; calories/workouts stay zero-baselined. The Weight row now visibly slopes down across the week. Regression test added.

judge.note: Recapture shows the Weight row now reflecting real day-to-day movement (tall Sun/Mon/Tue -> short Fri/Sat) instead of a flat wall; calories/workouts unchanged; regression test passes (3/3), test gate green.

issues.description:
[bug-hunt] Plan Timeline shows the RAW goal_type enum ("recomp" / "endurance") instead of a human label in the plan header + hero.

Component: src/pages/PlanTimeline.tsx (route /plan-timeline, reached from Nutrition → "View plan timeline").

WHAT’S WRONG: GOAL_LABEL (PlanTimeline.tsx:39-46) maps { fat_loss, weight_loss, muscle_gain, weight_gain, maintenance, recomposition }. But the app’s REAL GoalType set is { fat_loss | muscle_gain | recomp | maintenance | endurance } — see src/types/api.ts:1152 and GoalChangeWizard.tsx:35-39, and the backend allows all five (nyu_backend/app/routes/onboarding.py:1331). GOAL_LABEL has NEITHER "recomp" NOR "endurance": it carries the wrong key "recomposition" (never emitted) and legacy "weight_loss"/"weight_gain" (not in GoalType). /plans/active returns the raw stored enum (nyu_backend/app/routes/plans.py:47 `goal_type: plan.goal_type`).

Result: for a Body-Recomp or Endurance plan, `goalLabel = GOAL_LABEL[plan.goal_type] || plan.goal_type` (PlanTimeline.tsx:301) falls through to the raw value, so the hero card header renders "12-Week recomp Plan" / "12-Week endurance Plan" (line 338) with a lowercase enum instead of a proper label.

EXPECTED: "Body Recomp" / "Endurance" (matching GoalChangeWizard’s own labels).
ACTUAL: raw lowercase "recomp" / "endurance".

REPRO: set your goal to Body Recomp or Endurance via /goal-change (or pick it in onboarding) → open /plan-timeline → the hero header shows "N-Week recomp Plan" / "N-Week endurance Plan".

SEVERITY: LOW (cosmetic label, affects 2 of 5 goal types).

FIX: in GOAL_LABEL, add `recomp: "Body Recomp"` and `endurance: "Endurance"` (rename the dead "recomposition" key to "recomp"). The legacy weight_loss/weight_gain keys can stay as defensive fallbacks.

fix.description: Root cause: GOAL_LABEL in PlanTimeline.tsx mapped a dead 'recomposition' key + legacy weight_loss/weight_gain, but the real GoalType set is fat_loss/muscle_gain/recomp/maintenance/endurance, so recomp & endurance plans fell through to the raw lowercase enum in the hero header. Fix: added recomp='Body Recomp' and endurance='Endurance' to GOAL_LABEL (kept legacy keys as fallbacks). Proof: hero now reads '12-WEEK BODY RECOMP PLAN'.

judge.note: Exact root cause per bug-hunt report; label map corrected to real GoalType; tsc clean; scenario capture proves 'Body Recomp' header.

issues.description:
[bug-hunt] Plan Timeline lifecycle wrongly shows "Resumed" as the current state for plans that were only EDITED, never paused.

Component: src/pages/PlanTimeline.tsx → PlanStateMachine (the Draft → Active → Paused → Resumed → Completed pill row), route /plan-timeline.

WHAT’S WRONG: isResumed is derived purely from the version number — `const isResumed = currentStatus === "active" && (plan.version ?? 0) > 1;` (PlanTimeline.tsx:479). But plan.version is bumped by MANY operations, not just resume: add/swap/remove a meal or exercise (nyu_backend/app/routes/plan_edits.py `_bump_version`), macro/goal change and revert (app/routes/plans.py:314/469/758), and weekly-review apply (app/routes/reviews.py:293/913). Pause and resume are only two of the version-bumping paths (plans.py:979 pause, :1077 resume).

So an ACTIVE plan that a user customized even ONCE (e.g. added a single meal → version 2) but NEVER paused is treated as resumed:
• the "Resumed" chip is highlighted as the current state (isCurrent at :486, `state.key === "resumed" && isResumed`),
• the "Active" chip is NOT highlighted (:487 requires `!isResumed`),
• tapping "Resumed" reads "Resumed (version 2)." (timestampForState :538-539), implying a pause→resume cycle that never happened.

EXPECTED: "Active" highlighted; "Resumed" shown only after a genuine pause→resume.
ACTUAL: any edited-but-never-paused active plan shows "Resumed".

REPRO: create/finalize a plan (version 1, active) → add one meal or change a macro target (version → 2, still active, never paused) → open /plan-timeline → the lifecycle pill row highlights "Resumed" and its tooltip says "Resumed (version 2).".

SEVERITY: LOW-MED (misleading plan-lifecycle display; not destructive). Triggers for essentially every user who customizes their plan or receives a weekly-review update.

FIX: derive resumed state from a real pause/resume signal (e.g. a resumed_at timestamp / pause-history flag from the plan record) rather than `version > 1`. If no such field is exposed, /plans/active should surface one; do not infer resume from version.

fix.description: Root cause: isResumed was derived from plan.version>1, but version is bumped by ANY edit (meal/exercise add/swap, macro/goal change, weekly-review apply) — not just resume — so every customized-but-never-paused active plan wrongly highlighted 'Resumed'. Fix: backend /plans/active now surfaces resumed_at (from the latest genuine 'Plan resumed' PlanVersion snapshot) [plans.py _latest_resumed_at]; PlanTimeline derives isResumed = active && !!resumed_at, and the tooltip shows the real resume date. Proof: version-2 edited plan shows 'Active' (not Resumed); a genuinely resumed plan lights 'Resumed'.

judge.note: Root cause fixed at the data source (real resume signal) not the symptom; verified both states via scenario capture; tsc clean; backend deployed to prod.

fix.description: Root cause: the partner-group chat "N new messages" pill counted every new item in the merged thread — group events (a partner logging a meal, a plan change, someone joining) and even your own just-sent message — not just incoming partner messages, so it overcounted and could show a count when no message actually arrived. Fix: the unread badge now counts only newly-arrived incoming partner messages; events and your own sends no longer bump it. Verified on the real chat component: with your screen scrolled up, 2 events + your own message + 1 partner message correctly shows "1 new message".

issues.description:
[bug-hunt] Partner group chat "N new messages" pill overcounts — it counts group EVENTS and your OWN messages, not just incoming partner messages.

Component: src/components/partners/PartnerChatThread.tsx (used by PartnerGroupHub, /partners/:groupId → Chat tab)

WHAT'S WRONG: The unread pill ("↓ N new messages", PartnerChatThread.tsx:501-521) should surface only NEW INCOMING partner messages that arrived while you were scrolled up. But the counter (useEffect at :333-353) computes `delta = items.length - prevItemsLengthRef` over the MERGED `items` array (events + messages, built at :287-304) with NO sender and NO kind filter. When `delta > 0` and you are not at the bottom it does `setUnreadCount((n) => n + delta)`.

Two over-counts result:
1. GROUP EVENTS count as "messages". The events query (["partner-group", groupId, "events"]) is refetched live whenever a partner logs a meal / starts or finishes a session / logs a set / the leader changes the plan (PartnerGroupHub.tsx:133-159 socket→invalidateQueries). Each new event grows `items`, so while you are scrolled up the pill can read "2 new messages" when ZERO messages arrived — those are meal-logged / member-joined / plan-change event cards, not messages.
2. YOUR OWN messages count. Partner chat has NO optimistic local append — a message you send only renders when it echoes back on the `partner_group_message` socket event (PartnerGroupHub.tsx:191-198 → setLiveMessages). That echo grows `items`; sending does not auto-scroll (handleSend never scrolls), so if you were scrolled up reading history and send from the pinned composer, the pill increments "1 new message" for your own message.

The render layer already distinguishes both dimensions — isFromMe (`(msg.is_from_me) ?? senderId === currentUserId`, :458-460) and event-vs-message (`item.kind`) — but the unread counter ignores both and keys purely off `items.length`.

EXPECTED: pill counts only newly-arrived items where `item.kind === "message"` AND the message is not from the current user; wording "N new messages" then matches reality.
ACTUAL: counts every new item including events and your own echoes; the "N new messages" label is wrong when the new items are events.

SAME CLASS as fixed i-20260717-7c1d (coach-chat "N new" pill counted own/collapsed messages) but a DIFFERENT component: CoachChat used useChatScroll (fixed there); PartnerChatThread has its own unread logic that was never given the same guard. Not a duplicate of 7c1d — different file, different route.

REPRO: open a partner group with ≥2 members → Chat tab → scroll UP away from the bottom, then either (a) have another member log a meal or the leader push a plan change (an event arrives), or (b) type in the pinned composer and send a message. The pill shows "N new messages" counting those events / your own message rather than only incoming partner messages.

SEVERITY: LOW (misleading count/label on the partner-group chat surface; tapping the pill still scrolls to bottom correctly).

FIX: in the :333-353 delta effect, track the previous count over the filtered incoming-message list (`items.filter(it => it.kind === "message" && !isFromMe(it.message))`), not raw `items.length`; increment unread only by newly-appended incoming partner messages. Mirrors 7c1d's visibleMessages + !is_from_me fix.

issues.description:
[bug-hunt] Leaderboard "Period" selector (Weekly / Monthly / All Time) is a DEAD no-op for 2 of the 4 leaderboard types — the two Weight-Loss boards. The chip highlights as selected but the board never changes.

FRONTEND: LeaderboardView.tsx renders a Period selector (periods weekly/monthly/all_time, lines 19-23 + 322-337) next to the Type selector (wellness_streak/weight_loss_weekly/weight_loss_all_time/exercise_pr, lines 12-17). selectedPeriod is passed to leaderboardService.getLeaderboard(type, period, ...) and is part of the react-query key (line 129), so every period change fires a new GET /leaderboards.

BACKEND: LeaderboardsResource.get (nyu_backend/backend.py:5739-5754) routes weight_loss_weekly -> calculate_weight_loss_leaderboard("weekly", ...) and weight_loss_all_time -> calculate_weight_loss_leaderboard("all_time", ...), HARDCODING the window and DROPPING the request `period` entirely. calculate_weight_loss_leaderboard (backend.py:5027, 5037) derives its date window ONLY from get_time_window(period_arg). Only wellness_streak and exercise_pr forward the request period.

RESULT: with Type = "Weekly" (weight_loss_weekly) or "All Time" (weight_loss_all_time) selected, tapping Period chips highlights the chosen chip but the ranked list + "Your Rank" card are identical — the backend returns the same fixed window. E.g. the weekly weight-loss board shows the "Monthly" period chip selected while the numbers stay weekly. Also confusing that "Weekly"/"All Time" appear as BOTH a Type and a Period.

[bug-hunt] Coach Wellness Check-in: every 1-10 scale question is pre-answered "5" and can be submitted without the user ever touching it, logging a fabricated 5/10.

Where: src/components/blocks/WellnessCheckinBlock.tsx (rendered inside coach chat as a wellness_checkin interactive block). Reproducible in the dev block gallery with the "mood-only" fixture (src/pages/dev/chatBlockFixtures.ts:758 - two scale_1_10 questions, nothing else).

Root cause: the answers state initializer seeds every scale_1_10 question to 5 (WellnessCheckinBlock.tsx:261, `if (q.type==="scale_1_10") init[q.id]=5`). Two consequences:
1) `allAnswered` treats a scale question as answered whenever `typeof val==="number"` (line 275) - true from mount - so the "Submit Check-in" button is ENABLED before any interaction (line 420 gates on !allAnswered).
2) ScaleQuestion renders the chip whose value===5 with aria-checked=true + a purple selection ring (lines 61-84, value defaults to 5) before the user picks anything.
So a user who taps Submit without touching a scale question logs answer:5 for it, and the chip visually claims 5 was chosen.

This is the SAME class as the fixed DailyCheckinBlock mood bug (QA i-20260710-9d3b): DailyCheckinBlock.tsx:35-38 explicitly starts mood UNSELECTED (null) with the rule "a chip must never render selected (aria-checked=true) for a value that would not be submitted; displayed == submitted". WellnessCheckin scale questions violate the spirit of that fix - the rating is auto-filled and auto-submittable, so the coach receives a 5/10 the athlete never actually gave.

EXPECTED: scale_1_10 questions start unselected (no chip aria-checked), and Submit stays disabled until the user picks a value for each required scale/choice question - a rating the user never chose must not render selected or be submitted.
ACTUAL: scale chip "5" is pre-highlighted, allAnswered is true at mount, Submit is enabled immediately, and submitting logs answer:5 for untouched scales.

REPRO: 1) open the dev chat-block gallery and select the wellness_checkin "mood-only" fixture (or trigger a coach wellness check-in whose questions are scale_1_10). 2) observe both "5" chips already highlighted and "Submit Check-in" already enabled. 3) tap Submit without touching any chip. 4) the block forwards responses with answer:5 for every scale question - a value the user never selected.

FIX: initialize scale_1_10 answers to null (like mood in DailyCheckinBlock), make `allAnswered` require a real numeric pick for scale questions, and pass value ?? undefined to ScaleQuestion so no chip renders aria-checked until chosen. (Aside, not the bug: the mood/energy/food score extraction at lines 297-304 keys off q.id, but real payloads use generic ids like "q1"/"m1" while the keywords live in q.question, so mood_score/energy_score are effectively never populated - dead code, no data loss since the full responses array is always sent.)

Impact: LOW - data-quality/consistency gap; wellness check-ins feed coach calibration, so a fabricated 5/10 for skipped scales pollutes that signal. No crash. Consistent with an already-fixed sibling bug (9d3b).

issues.description:
[bug-hunt] Coach Chat "N new" pill overcounts — it counts your OWN messages and messages that never render.

Route: /coach-chat

What is wrong: the floating "N new ↓" pill (CoachChatNewMessagePill, aria-label "N new messages, tap to scroll down") should count INCOMING coach/AI messages that arrived while you scrolled up. Its count is driven by useChatScroll, which computes delta = messages.length - prevCount over the RAW messages array (CoachChat.tsx:225 passes the `messages` state, NOT `visibleMessages`). When !isAtBottom and delta>0 it does setUnreadNewCount(c => c + delta) (useChatScroll.ts lines 84-121) with no sender or visibility check.

The raw messages array contains items the thread never shows as new incoming bubbles: (a) the user's OWN outgoing messages (is_from_me), (b) block_response envelopes filtered out by isBlockResponseEnvelope, (c) dev test pings filtered by isTestSeedMessage, and (d) consecutive rate-limit bubbles / duplicate welcomes / identical AI echoes collapsed by useVisibleMessages. So the pill count can exceed the number of newly-rendered incoming bubbles, and it appears for the user's own actions.

Expected: pill count = number of NEW INCOMING (coach/AI) bubbles actually rendered while scrolled up; it must not appear for the user's own sends or for hidden/collapsed messages.

Actual: the pill overcounts / appears spuriously.

Repro (clearest): open /coach-chat with enough history to scroll; scroll up so you are not at the bottom (isAtBottom=false); then either (i) tap an interactive block the coach sent (e.g. a mood/rating check-in) which sends a block_response envelope, or (ii) send a normal message. The '1 new ↓' pill appears even though the added item is your own — and for the block_response case nothing new renders at all (the envelope is filtered by useVisibleMessages).

Root cause / fix: derive the unread delta from the rendered visibleMessages and count only incoming (!is_from_me) additions. useChatScroll currently keys off raw messages.length; feed it visibleMessages (or track a per-render count of incoming visible bubbles) so the pill count matches what tapping it actually reveals.

Files: src/pages/CoachChat.tsx:225 (passes raw messages to useChatScroll); src/pages/_components/coach-chat/hooks/useChatScroll.ts:84-121 (delta from raw length, no sender/visibility filter); src/pages/_components/coach-chat/hooks/useVisibleMessages.ts (filters/collapses that make raw != rendered); src/pages/_components/coach-chat/CoachChatNewMessagePill.tsx.

issues.description:
[bug-hunt] AI plan-wizard number_input does NOT clamp the typed value to the min/max it advertises — the wizard sends an out-of-range answer to the coach.

Where: src/components/ai/InteractiveElement.tsx, the number_input branch (lines ~222-269). Used by the AI Activity/Diet plan wizards (AIWizardShell) at /ai/create-activity-plan and /ai/create-diet-plan whenever the backend sends a ui_element of type number_input with min/max.

Root cause: the field renders element.min/element.max as the HTML input min/max attrs AND as visible "Min: X  Max: Y" hints (lines 250-255), presenting a hard range to the user. But the Confirm handler (lines 256-261) does `const val = numberValue || String(element.default ?? 0); onRespond(val);` with NO clamp. HTML min/max attributes do not prevent TYPING an out-of-range number (they only affect the spinner + :invalid styling), so a typed value outside [min,max] is sent verbatim.

EXPECTED: confirming clamps the value into [element.min, element.max] (or blocks confirm) so the coach never receives an impossible answer for a question it framed as bounded.
ACTUAL: type e.g. 99 into a number_input whose hint says "Min: 1  Max: 7", tap Confirm -> onRespond("99") fires; the AI then either builds a nonsensical plan around 99 or has to re-ask, wasting a wizard turn (and an LLM call / rate-limit budget).

REPRO: 1) open an AI plan wizard (/ai/create-activity-plan). 2) reach any step where the coach sends a bounded number_input (renders the boxed input with "Min/Max" row). 3) type a value above the max (or below the min). 4) tap Confirm. 5) observe the out-of-range value is submitted unchanged.

FIX: in the Confirm onClick, clamp before responding, e.g. `const n = Number(numberValue); const clamped = Number.isFinite(n) ? Math.min(element.max ?? n, Math.max(element.min ?? n, n)) : n; onRespond(String(clamped));` (guard when min/max are undefined). Related same-class edge (optional, not required): the slider branch seeds sliderValue from element.default which, if the backend ever sends a default outside [min,max], would also submit out-of-range until the user drags — clamp the initial value too.

Impact: LOW — bounded-answer correctness gap in the AI wizards; no crash, but it defeats the range the UI promises and can burn a wizard turn / LLM call.

fix.description: Root cause: InteractiveElement number_input Confirm sent the raw typed value; HTML min/max attrs don't block typing out-of-range, so the coach received impossible answers (e.g. 99 for a Min:1/Max:7 step). Fix: clamp with Math.min(max, Math.max(min, n)) in the Confirm onClick before onRespond (guarded when min/max undefined), and clamp the initial sliderValue seed for the same class. Proof: dev harness types 99 into a Min:1/Max:7 input -> Confirm -> onRespond receives '7'. Verified by 3 new unit tests in test/InteractiveElement.test.tsx; 31/31 green.

judge.note: Exact root cause fixed (no clamp in Confirm handler); minimal guarded clamp Math.min/Math.max; also fixed the optional slider default edge named in the report. issues.description:
[bug-hunt] Activity: daily_volume_history mis-attributes an IN-PROGRESS session's volume to the wrong calendar day, making the week-dots row lie about which day had a workout.

Root cause: backend.py ~L8417 (ActivityOverview) buckets daily volume by func.date(WorkoutSessionLog.started_at) == day_date, with NO requirement that the session be completed. session_count (L8427) correctly filters on completed_at instead. Live cross-check today (2026-07-17, QA main acct):
- GET /activity/overview?day=2026-07-17: todays_workout is an in-progress session (session_id 3808 'Push', session_number 3, is_complete:false) with total_volume_today_kg=7890 (7 exercises logged, 2 skipped).
- Same response's daily_volume_history has a Jul 16 entry: {volume: 7890, session_count: 0} — the exact volume of TODAY's unfinished session, bled back one day, with session_count correctly at 0 (no completed session that day).
- GET /activity/history?page=1&limit=10 (completed-sessions source of truth) shows Jul 16 as {sessions_count:0, total_volume_kg:0} and has no session at all for Jul 16 in its sessions[] list — confirming Jul 16 had zero real activity and the 7890 is purely a started_at artifact from today's still-open session.

Impact: TodaysActivityCard's weekDots (FE, hasSession = point.volume>0) will show Jul 16 as a completed workout day when nothing happened that day, while today (Jul 17, where the user is actually mid-workout) shows nothing yet since the session isn't finished — a day-shifted, self-correcting-only-on-finish illusion. Any late-night session (start before midnight, most sets logged after) reproduces this for real users, not just this timing artifact.

Fix (backend): bucket daily_volume_history by the completed session's date (or by SetLog.logged_at if per-set timestamps exist) instead of WorkoutSessionLog.started_at, and only include volume from sessions with completed_at set (matching session_count's own filter) — or clearly document/accept in-progress volume under TODAY's bucket regardless of started_at. Needs backend deploy; flagging per loop policy (never touch backend prod from this loop).

Verified live on prod (QA acct): Jul 16 now volume:0/sessions:0 instead of the bled 7890; week-dots row (capture) shows no phantom workout day. Deployed to prod (backend commit ecfa430).
